title: Cross-team reliability capacity simulation and ops compact
content:
Purpose and context:
We need a compact, actionable cross-team plan to validate that proposed SLO target sets and capacity policies are operationally achievable across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. This doc records a small-run experiment (6 weeks) combining traffic simulation, ops tabletop, and a lightweight rollout plan so org stakeholders can confirm investment decisions for Dedicated capacity and automated fallback policies.

Intended audience:
- SRE leads, platform engineering, serving-runtime owners
- Product managers for Hosted API and Dedicated
- Solutions and Support leads who will own customer escalations
- Observability and release engineers who will run the simulations and telemetry checks

High-level objectives (what success looks like):
1) Validate that the 99th percentile latency SLO for text-generation (95% of request mix) can be met with proposed Dedicated autoscaling policy on standard cluster shapes under two synthetic load profiles.
2) Exercise model fallback and routing logic end-to-end in staging with observable roll-forward/rollback triggers and runbook steps documented.
3) Produce an ops compact: 1-page runbook summary + escalation matrix + three remediation playbooks (cache warm, scale, and degrade-gracefully).
4) Produce clear capacity delta estimates (GPU hours, burst headroom) and an error-budget burn model tied to business impact levels.

Scope and exclusions:
- In scope: text-generation and chat endpoints; both streaming and non-streaming; both hosted and dedicated stacks on the cluster shapes we own today. Include KV caching behavior and batching profiles.
- Out of scope: embeddings endpoints for this experiment; long-sequence offline finetuning; private air-gapped installs (we will do a follow-up run if needed).

Experiment phases and schedule (6 weeks):
Week 0 (prep, owner: Platform Eng): finalize simulation harness, select replay traces, seed test clusters with representative models (small, medium, large).
Week 1 (baseline runs, owner: Observability): run graceful-stress baseline (no fallbacks) to measure current latency distribution and resource saturation points.
Week 2 (autoscale policy validation, owner: Serving Runtime): apply proposed autoscale rules, warm caches, capture P95/P99, measure scale-up latency.
Week 3 (failure injection and fallback, owner: SRE): inject node preemption and regional capacity constraints; validate smart routing to fallback model variants and measure user-visible latency and quality delta.
Week 4 (tabletop & runbook rehearsal, owner: Product/Support): cross-team tabletop sim where oncall follows ops compact and records gaps.
Week 5 (postmortem and cost delta estimate, owner: Finance liaison): consolidate telemetry, compute GPU-hour delta, recommended commits for Dedicated.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Experiment lead: Aisha Patel (SRE) — coordinator, central verdict owner.
- Platform engineering: build and provision test cluster shapes, coordinate quotas.
- Serving runtime: implement autoscale hooks and timing metrics; instrument kernel-selection traces.
- Observability: create dashboards, capture histograms, produce error-budget projection workbook.
- Product (Hosted API/Dedicated PM): define SLO acceptance thresholds and business impact levels.
- Support/Solutions: participate in tabletop, own customer-facing messaging templates.

SLOs under test (proposed definitions for the experiment):
- Latency SLO (interactive text-gen): 99th percentile server-side latency <= 450ms for 95% of production traffic mix.
- Availability SLO: Success rate >= 99.9% (errors defined as 5xx and client timeouts) per 30d window, with a 0.1% monthly error budget for critical customers.
- Degradation SLO: Under capacity constraint, fallback to lower-capacity model must preserve success rate >= 99.0 and median latency <= 700ms.

Measurement plan and telemetry signals:
- Primary signals: request latency distribution (P50/P95/P99), GPU utilization per-instance, queue depth, pending-batch size, KV cache hit rate, model-switch frequency.
- Secondary signals: token-per-second cost estimate, per-token error patterns (timeout vs OOM), trace-level tail latencies.
- Alert thresholds: pre-wired alerts on P99 > 400ms sustained 5m, GPU util > 85% for 10m, cache-hit < 60% drop.

Runbooks to produce (deliverables):
1) Ops compact one-pager: immediate checklist for oncall (detect -> mitigate -> escalate).
2) Scale playbook: exact steps to add capacity, verify health, validate SLO return.
3) Cache recovery playbook: steps to warm prefixes + force reuse across replicas.
4) Graceful-degrade playbook: how to enable fallback routing, update client-facing headers, and record quality telemetry.

Tabletop scenarios (short examples):
- Scenario A: Sudden 3x traffic surge for 20 minutes originating from a single region; autoscaler stalls for 90 seconds. Walkthrough the degrade playbook.
- Scenario B: Node preemption hits 30% of a dedicated pool; verify routing to Dedicated-burst and hosted fallback.
- Scenario C: Cache corruption event causing KV-hit collapse; practice cache-warm playbook + rollback.

Risk heatmap (quick notes):
- High risk: fallback model introduces unacceptable hallucination on a small but critical prompt-set. Mitigation: pre-run prompt regressions and tie regression alarms to rollout gates.
- Medium risk: autoscale lag causes short error budget burns. Mitigation: conservative burst capacity and request shed policy.
- Low risk: telemetry gaps (missing token-level cost) — fix during baseline week.

Decision gates and acceptance criteria:
Gate 1 (end of week 2): P99 baseline with autoscale policy must be within 20% of target SLO; otherwise iterate config.
Gate 2 (end of week 3): Fallback must keep success rate >= 99.0 on injected failures; if not, we do a focused engineering sprint.
Gate 3 (end of week 5): Cost delta estimate must be within 15% of finance projection and error-budget burn acceptable for a pilot cohort.

Communication and cadence:
- Weekly 30m sync: experiment lead + leads from each function (Platform, Serving, Observability, Support, Product).
- Daily Slack channel (#reliability-cap-sim) for run updates during active weeks. Postmortem doc created in Confluence with linked artifacts.

Open questions / unknowns:
- What is the acceptable quality delta (automatic vs manual) for fallback models on customer SLAs? (product to define).
- Can Dedicated autoscale add warm GPUs faster than 45s? Need infra measurement.
- Is there a safe token-cost proxy we can compute in realtime for cost-aware routing?

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Platform: provision two test clusters (one matching small-prod, one matching dedicated-shape) — due EOD Tue.
- Observability: clone main latency dashboard and add experiment traces — due Wed.
- Serving runtime: merge autoscale hook PR to staging and enable in test clusters — due Thu.
- Product: finalize business-impact mapping and the critical prompt-set for hallucination checks — due Fri.

Appendix: quick template for the ops compact one-pager (to be filled):
- Title: Experiment compact — Detect / Triage / Mitigate / Escalate
- Detect: primary alerts and dashboards to watch
- Triage: first 4 checks (is it regional, is it model-specific, is it cache-related, is it infra?)
- Mitigate: step-by-step immediate actions (route to fallback, scale pool, enable shed) + how to annotate telemetry
- Escalate: who to call at each severity with phone and slack tags

Notes to reviewers:
This is intentionally compact and pragmatic: objective is a run, learn, and decide cycle. Please add comments directly in the doc or on the linked Jira (REL-1023) if you want additional scenarios or scope adjustments.

Signed: Aisha Patel (experiment lead)
